bottom_line: In RE-DUAL PCI, dual therapy with dabigatran 110 mg plus a P2Y12 inhibitor resulted in a lower incidence of the primary end point than triple therapy with warfarin (hazard ratio, 0.52; 95% CI, 0.42 to 0.63).
implications: Based on the reported primary end-point rates and hazard ratio (15.4% vs 26.9%; hazard ratio, 0.52; 95% CI, 0.42 to 0.63), the results support that dabigatran 110-mg dual therapy was associated with lower major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding than warfarin-based triple therapy in this trial; based on the composite efficacy end point (13.7% vs 13.4%; hazard ratio, 1.04; 95% CI, 0.84 to 1.29; P = 0.005 for noninferiority), the data support noninferiority for that composite when dual-therapy groups were combined, but do not establish superiority for efficacy.
